title: Potential from a larger charge
hook: Change source charge magnitude and predict electric-potential magnitude.
misconception: electric-potential magnitude stays fixed when source charge magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r to compare electric-potential magnitude when source charge magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a point charge at fixed distance with zero potential at infinity, potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r. When source charge magnitude doubles, electric-potential magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a point charge at fixed distance with zero potential at infinity, with a nonzero initial result. If source charge magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-potential magnitude?
recall.why: Apply potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
